chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Bukayr, from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who assumed a guarantee (debt), then settled (compounded) on part of what he had settled on. He said: 'He is entitled only to what he settled on.'

key_terms.ضَمِنَ: Assumed a guarantee or became liable for a debt

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for a guarantor who settles a debt for less than the full amount?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifying that a guarantor (*damin*) who compounds a settlement (*sulh*) with the creditor is entitled to recover only the actual amount paid, preventing unjust enrichment. This principle underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness in financial transactions, ensuring the guarantor’s recourse matches their actual loss rather than the original principal. It highlights the legal distinction between simple guarantee and negotiated settlement in Islamic commercial law.
